reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a Coinbase signup promotion directing viewers to create an account, verify their identity, and complete a qualifying crypto purchase or trade for a possible reward. It discloses that the promoter may receive a commission from purchases through the links, and describes the reward claim and link as ordinary promotional content with conditions rather than deceptive conduct.

citations.quote: This link automatically applies the current Coinbase promotion. No coupon code required — using the link ensures you're eligible for any available new-user bonus.
You typically have to create a new account, verify your identity, and complete a qualifying crypto purchase before the reward is credited to your account.
complete your first qualifying trade and your reward will be added automatically once the requirements are met.
Some promotions advertise rewards of up to $200 in crypto, although the actual bonus amount usually depends on the size of your first purchase and the current promotion.
when you make a purchase through our links, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

opening.argument: The video links a promised crypto reward directly to a sequence of actions that benefits the promoter: viewers are directed to use the description or pinned-comment link, create an account, verify identity, and make a qualifying purchase. The offer is therefore not merely informational; it is a solicitation for registration, identity disclosure, and a financial transaction in exchange for an advertised reward. The supposed automatic activation does not remove the risk that viewers are being induced to act through an external link before they know whether they qualify.

citations.quote: This link automatically applies the current Coinbase promotion. No coupon code required — using the link ensures you're eligible for any available new-user bonus.
You typically have to create a new account, verify your identity, and complete a qualifying crypto purchase before the reward is credited to your account.
when you make a purchase through our links, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an ordinary promotion does not answer the central concern: the viewer is urged to follow an external link, create an account, verify identity, and purchase crypto to pursue a reward. The commission disclosure confirms that the speaker benefits when viewers use the links, while the cited conditions show that the reward is contingent rather than assured. A conditional solicitation can still be deceptive if the headline incentive drives financial action before eligibility and value are clear.

citations.quote: when you make a purchase through our links, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.
complete a qualifying crypto purchase before the reward is credited to your account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument establishes a disclosed affiliate relationship and a conditional promotion, but it does not establish fraud, a fake reward, or loss caused by the link. The materials expressly say the reward depends on the current promotion and qualifying requirements, and the purchase is described as something a viewer may already intend to make. Those facts are consistent with ordinary promotional referral content, not proof that the solicitation is deceptive.

citations.quote: the actual bonus amount usually depends on the size of your first purchase and the current promotion.
complete your first qualifying trade and your reward will be added automatically once the requirements are met.

opening.argument: The presentation combines several high-risk signals: a crypto reward, a sign-up prompt, a required purchase, and language suggesting an easy automatic benefit. The page shown in the video advertises, “Earn up to $2,000 when you buy $50 in crypto,” while the narration separately discusses rewards of up to around $200. That discrepancy makes the headline incentive especially difficult for a viewer to evaluate. The offer is framed around a small purchase unlocking a much larger digital-asset reward, yet the actual qualification and reward amount remain dependent on undisclosed current terms.

citations.quote: some campaigns advertise rewards of up to around $200 in crypto FOR NEW users depending on the promotion and trading activity.
the bonus usually requires a few simple steps.
your reward will be added automatically once the requirements are met.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the conditions as reassuring, but conditions do not resolve the unusually strong visual promise. The video shows a $2,000 headline tied to buying $50, whereas the narration mentions approximately $200 and says the result depends on trading activity. Presenting the largest figure prominently while relegating uncertainty to qualifications can make the offer appear easier and more valuable than the available explanation supports.

citations.quote: some campaigns advertise rewards of up to around $200 in crypto FOR NEW users depending on the promotion and trading activity.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual headline itself says “up to,” and the narration expressly qualifies the amount by promotion and trading activity. The evidence therefore shows variable promotional terms, not a guaranteed return or proof that the headline is false. The purchase is a qualifying condition for a possible reward, and the materials do not claim that every buyer receives the maximum amount.

citations.quote: Some promotions advertise rewards of up to $200 in crypto, although the actual bonus amount usually depends on the size of your first purchase and the current promotion.
although the average reward is often much smaller than the headline.

opening.argument: Although presented as an explanation of how discounts work, the video functions as a direct promotional funnel. Its title centers on a new-user promotion, the description repeats the same link, and the narration tells viewers to use that link to activate eligibility. The speaker also acknowledges receiving a commission from purchases through the links. That combination shows the educational framing is serving a participation objective: viewers are guided toward Coinbase registration and a qualifying crypto trade rather than given a neutral review of whether they should participate.

citations.quote: Coinbase Discount 2026 – New User Promotion + How It Works
this video explains how Coinbase promotions actually work and how to activate the current Coinbase new-user bonus before creating your account
If you're going to open a Coinbase account anyway, you can use the link in the description or the pinned comment so you're eligible for any current new user promotions after your first trade.
when you make a purchase through our links, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The claim that this is merely educational overlooks the repeated call to use the description or pinned-comment link and the admitted commission. Explaining steps can make a solicitation more effective; it does not make it neutral. The video directs viewers toward account creation and a first trade while presenting the link as the way to obtain eligibility, so its practical function is promotion regardless of the explanatory wording.

citations.quote: the easiest way to get the current Coinbase discount is by using the link in the pinned comment or description
This link automatically applies the current Coinbase promotion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotional intent is not itself evidence of a scam. The materials identify the subject as a new-user promotion, explain that identity verification and a qualifying purchase are required, and disclose the possible commission. The argument shows that the video encourages participation, but it does not show that the link is fraudulent, that the reward is guaranteed, or that the stated conditions are concealed.
